The present invention discloses a preparation method of a Cu-based resistive random access memory, and a memory. The preparation method includes: performing composition and a chemical combination treatment on a lower copper electrode (10) to generate a compound buffer layer (40), wherein the compound buffer layer (40) is capable of preventing the oxidation of the lower copper electrode (10); depositing a solid electrolyte material (50) on the compound buffer layer (40); and depositing an upper electrode (60) on the solid electrolyte material (50) to form the memory. In the above technical solution, the compound buffer layer (40) capable of preventing the oxidation of the lower copper electrode (10) is inserted between the lower copper electrode (10) and the solid electrolyte material (50) to efficiently prevent the oxidation of the lower copper electrode (10) in a growth process of the solid electrolyte material (50), such that an electrode interface does not become rough due to the oxidation, thereby solving the technical problem of relatively low reliability and yield of the device resulting from the rough electrode interface of the Cu-based resistive random access memory in the prior art, and thus the reliability and the yield of the device are improved.

The present invention discloses a method for preparing a Cu-based resistive random access memory and a memory fabricated thereby. The preparation method includes: performing composition and chemical combination treatment on a lower copper electrode (10) to form a compound buffer layer (40), wherein the compound buffer layer (40) is capable of preventing oxidation of the lower copper electrode (10); depositing a solid electrolyte material (50) on the compound buffer layer (40); and depositing an upper electrode (60) on the solid electrolyte material (50) to form the memory.

In the above technical solution, the compound buffer layer (40), which is capable of preventing oxidation of the lower copper electrode (10), is inserted between the lower copper electrode (10) and the solid electrolyte material (50). This effectively prevents oxidation of the lower copper electrode (10) during the growth process of the solid electrolyte material (50), thereby preventing the electrode interface from becoming rough due to oxidation. Accordingly, the technical problem in the prior art, namely the relatively low reliability and yield of Cu-based resistive random access memory devices caused by rough electrode interfaces, is solved, thereby improving both the reliability and yield of the device.

A method for manufacturing a copper-based resistive random access memory device, as well as the resulting memory, is described. The method involves treating a lower copper electrode (10) through compositional adjustment and chemical bonding so as to form a compound buffer layer (40). This compound buffer layer (40) can inhibit oxidation of the lower copper electrode (10). A solid electrolyte material (50) is then formed on the compound buffer layer (40), after which an upper electrode (60) is deposited over the solid electrolyte material (50) to complete the memory structure.

With this approach, the compound buffer layer (40), which protects the lower copper electrode (10) from oxidation, is positioned between the lower copper electrode (10) and the solid electrolyte material (50). As a result, oxidation of the lower copper electrode (10) during formation of the solid electrolyte material (50) is effectively suppressed. This prevents the electrode interface from becoming uneven because of oxidation, thereby addressing the prior-art issue in which a rough electrode interface in copper-based resistive random access memory devices leads to reduced device reliability and production yield. Consequently, both the reliability and yield of the device are enhanced.
outputs.L3:
The invention relates to a method for preparing a copper-based resistive random access memory, as well as to the memory device obtained by this method.

In the preparation process, a lower copper electrode is first formed. The surface of the lower copper electrode is then treated to form a compound buffer layer. This compound buffer layer is provided between the lower copper electrode and a subsequently formed solid electrolyte layer, and serves to protect the copper electrode from oxidation.

After formation of the compound buffer layer, a solid electrolyte material is deposited on the compound buffer layer. An upper electrode is then deposited on the solid electrolyte material, thereby completing the basic memory cell structure. The resulting device therefore includes, in sequence, a lower copper electrode, a compound buffer layer, a solid electrolyte layer, and an upper electrode.

The compound buffer layer plays an important role during fabrication. In particular, it prevents or significantly reduces oxidation of the lower copper electrode during growth or deposition of the solid electrolyte material. Without such protection, the lower copper electrode may be oxidized, which can cause undesirable changes at the interface between the electrode and the solid electrolyte.

By preventing oxidation of the lower copper electrode, the compound buffer layer helps maintain a smoother and more stable interface. This reduces interface roughness and improves the structural quality of the memory cell. As a result, the resistive random access memory device can exhibit improved reliability, enhanced process stability, and increased production yield.
outputs.L4:
A copper-based resistive random access memory (ReRAM) device is fabricated using a process that protects the copper electrode during formation of the memory stack. First, a lower electrode made of copper or a copper-containing conductive material is prepared on a substrate. The exposed surface of this lower copper electrode is then chemically treated so that a thin compound buffer layer is formed directly on the copper surface. This buffer layer is selected to suppress oxidation of the copper and to act as a stable interface between the copper electrode and the subsequently deposited memory material.

After formation of the buffer layer, a solid electrolyte layer is deposited over the treated lower electrode. The solid electrolyte may be an insulating or ion-conductive material capable of supporting copper ion migration and conductive filament formation during device operation. An upper electrode is then formed on the solid electrolyte layer to complete the resistive memory cell structure.

The chemically formed buffer layer plays an important role in improving device performance and manufacturability. During deposition of the solid electrolyte, an untreated copper surface can easily oxidize or become roughened, which may lead to an unstable electrode/electrolyte interface. Such interface degradation can cause variations in switching voltage, poor retention, reduced endurance, leakage current, and lower production yield. By preventing or reducing copper oxidation and suppressing interface roughening, the buffer layer provides a smoother and more chemically stable interface.

As a result, the Cu-based ReRAM device can exhibit more uniform resistive switching characteristics, improved reliability, and enhanced fabrication yield. The method is particularly useful for memory devices in which copper serves as an active electrode material and where precise control of the electrode/electrolyte interface is important for stable device operation.

**The Power of “The”**

“The” may be one of the smallest and most common words in the English language, but it plays an important role in communication. It is called the definite article, and it helps us refer to something specific. For example, when we say “a book,” we could mean any book. But when we say “the book,” we mean a particular book that both the speaker and listener understand.

This simple word gives clarity and direction. It helps identify people, places, objects, and ideas. “The sun,” “the ocean,” and “the truth” all feel more precise because of this tiny word. Without “the,” many sentences would sound incomplete or unclear.

Although it is often overlooked, “the” is essential in everyday language. It shows that even the smallest words can have great importance. In writing and speaking, “the” helps shape meaning, making our thoughts easier to understand.

counterfactuals.output: An invention relates to a fabrication method for a copper-based resistive random access memory device. The compound buffer layer is configured to isolate the lower copper electrode from an oxidizing atmosphere or oxidizing species during subsequent processing, thereby suppressing oxidation of the lower copper electrode before formation of the solid electrolyte layer and upper electrode. As a result, the fabricated resistive random access memory device exhibits improved interface stability, reduced process-induced degradation, and enhanced switching reliability.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a patent-style summary describing a preparation method for Cu-based RRAM that treats the lower Cu electrode to form an anti-oxidation compound buffer layer, then deposits electrolyte material and an upper electrode, emphasizing improved reliability and yield.
counterfactuals.output:
A preparation method for a Cu-based resistive random access memory (RRAM) device is provided. The method includes forming a lower copper electrode on a substrate, subjecting a surface region of the lower copper electrode to a treatment process to convert at least part of the exposed copper surface into an anti-oxidation compound buffer layer, depositing an electrolyte material layer on the anti-oxidation compound buffer layer, and forming an upper electrode on the electrolyte material layer.

In one implementation, the lower electrode comprises copper or a copper-containing conductive layer formed by sputtering, evaporation, electroplating, chemical vapor deposition, or a damascene process. After the lower electrode is exposed, the surface treatment may include reacting the copper surface with a sulfur-containing, nitrogen-containing, halogen-containing, carbon-containing, oxygen-controlled, or other compound-forming atmosphere or solution, thereby forming a thin copper compound layer. The copper compound layer may include, for example, copper sulfide, copper nitride, copper halide, copper carbide, copper oxide of controlled thickness and composition, or an organic/inorganic copper complex layer. The buffer layer is preferably sufficiently thin to maintain electrical conduction and ion migration capability while acting as a protective interface.

The electrolyte material is then deposited over the treated lower electrode. The electrolyte may comprise a solid electrolyte, chalcogenide material, oxide material, nitride material, polymer electrolyte, or other ion-conducting switching medium suitable for Cu-based conductive-bridge memory operation. The upper electrode may comprise an inert metal, such as Pt, W, TiN, TaN, Au, or another conductive material, or may comprise an active electrode depending on device design.

By forming the anti-oxidation compound buffer layer prior to electrolyte deposition, uncontrolled oxidation of the lower Cu electrode during subsequent processing and storage is suppressed. The buffer layer stabilizes the Cu/electrolyte interface, reduces interfacial defects and variability, inhibits excessive copper diffusion or corrosion, and improves adhesion and film uniformity. As a result, Cu ion injection during set/reset operation becomes more controllable, reducing cycle-to-cycle and cell-to-cell variation.

The disclosed preparation method therefore improves the switching reliability, retention stability, endurance characteristics, and production yield of Cu-based RRAM devices. The method is compatible with conventional semiconductor fabrication processes and may be applied to single-cell devices, cross-point arrays, embedded nonvolatile memory structures, and integrated logic-memory systems.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate the “present invention discloses…” section for a memory device patent: lower copper electrode (10), compound buffer layer (40), solid electrolyte material (50), upper electrode (60), and explain how the buffer layer solves rough interface problems caused by oxidation.
counterfactuals.output:
The present invention discloses a memory device comprising a lower copper electrode (10), a compound buffer layer (40) formed on the lower copper electrode (10), a solid electrolyte material layer (50) formed on the compound buffer layer (40), and an upper electrode (60) formed on the solid electrolyte material layer (50).

In the memory device of the present invention, the lower copper electrode (10) serves as an active electrode capable of supplying copper ions during operation of the memory device. The solid electrolyte material layer (50) is configured to permit migration of the copper ions under an applied electric field, thereby enabling formation and rupture of a conductive path between the lower copper electrode (10) and the upper electrode (60). Accordingly, the memory device may perform resistance switching between a low-resistance state and a high-resistance state.

The compound buffer layer (40) is disposed between the lower copper electrode (10) and the solid electrolyte material layer (50). The compound buffer layer (40) functions as an interface control layer for improving the surface condition of the lower copper electrode (10) before formation of the solid electrolyte material layer (50). In particular, when the lower copper electrode (10) is exposed to an oxidizing atmosphere or an oxygen-containing process environment, oxidation of copper may occur at the surface of the lower copper electrode (10). Such oxidation can form copper oxide or other non-uniform reaction products, resulting in a rough interface, increased interfacial defects, non-uniform ion injection, and unstable resistance switching characteristics.

According to the present invention, the compound buffer layer (40) suppresses or mitigates the adverse effects of oxidation at the surface of the lower copper electrode (10). The compound buffer layer (40) covers and stabilizes the surface of the lower copper electrode (10), thereby reducing direct reaction between the copper electrode and the solid electrolyte material layer (50). The compound buffer layer (40) may further planarize or smooth the interface, compensate for surface irregularities caused by copper oxidation, and provide a chemically stable transition region between the lower copper electrode (10) and the solid electrolyte material layer (50).

As a result, the interface between the lower copper electrode (10) and the solid electrolyte material layer (50) is made more uniform. The compound buffer layer (40) prevents localized protrusions, voids, or rough oxide regions from acting as uncontrolled ion injection sites. Consequently, formation of the conductive filament or conductive path in the solid electrolyte material layer (50) becomes more controllable and reproducible. The memory device therefore exhibits improved switching uniformity, reduced variation in set and reset voltages, enhanced endurance, and improved retention reliability.

In one embodiment, the compound buffer layer (40) is formed of a compound material capable of maintaining interfacial stability with copper while allowing controlled migration or injection of copper ions into the solid electrolyte material layer (50). The compound buffer layer (40) may include an oxide, nitride, oxynitride, sulfide, or other compound layer selected to reduce surface roughness and suppress excessive oxidation of the lower copper electrode (10). The thickness of the compound buffer layer (40) may be selected so that the layer is sufficiently thick to improve interfacial uniformity while remaining sufficiently thin to permit memory switching operation.

Accordingly, the present invention provides a memory device in which the compound buffer layer (40) is interposed between the lower copper electrode (10) and the solid electrolyte material layer (50), thereby solving the problem of a rough and defective interface caused by oxidation of the lower copper electrode (10), and improving the electrical reliability and switching stability of the memory device.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3
